reports.note: Multiple reports of trees down and property damage around the Ramsey Street and Linden intersection. Potential start of a tornado track.

EF-1 tornado confirmed. Touched down in the Stone Ridge neighborhood, with a discontinuous path of tree and structural damage northward into the Neuse Crossing neighborhood. Total path length of 2.5 miles, with a peak width of 150 yards, and a duration of 5 minutes.

NWS survey team confirmed an EF-2 tornado in northeastern Newberry County. The tornado touched down near or just before the intersection of Old Blair Road and Henderson Ferry Road where it snapped branches of multiple pine trees and uprooted or snapped several other pines. The tornado crossed the clearing and followed Old Blair Road, snapping and uprooting various hardwood and softwood trees. A home located off of Old Blair Road had several large pine trees snapped or uprooted around the property. There was a small camper on the property which was flipped. As the tornado continued northeastward towards the Broad River it reached the maximum intensity with peak winds estimated to be 115 mph. Much of the forested area along Old Blair Road was destroyed with numerous snapped pine trees found along and north of the road. The trees also brought down several power poles after falling on the poles or attached lines. The tornado lifted just before reaching the Broad River.
Live stream showed active tornado on the ground, causing trees to be shredded and debris to be lofted. Roof and siding were also ripped off manufactured home, and power lines were snapped.
Public reported 4 structures destroyed on property with power outage and power line snapped.

Approximate starting point of confirmed EF-1 tornado. A tornado touched down southwest of Louisburg, NC and moved to the northeast before crossing NC-56 just west of Timberlake Rd before dissipating. Mostly tree damage, with some structural and fencing damage was observed, consistent with an EF-1 tornado. Preliminary total path length of 1.93 miles, with a peak width of 130 yards, and a duration of 5 minutes.

NWS Survey Team confirmed an EF-1 tornado in western Allendale Co. The tornado crossed Hwy 301 west of Gravel Hill Rd, causing significant damage. 4 homes were impacted: one sustained destruction of aluminum roofing material and a front porch; one had complete roof & outer wall failure on a rear addition; & 2 sustained minor roof damage. An outbuilding & 2 carports were destroyed. The tornado continued north with additional tree damage west of Moultry Loop and on Revolutionary Trail.
Storm Spotters reported tornado northwest on Barnwell along 278. Radar confirmed debris as well.

Aiken County EM relayed a report of two downed trees. One near the interaction of Coleman Bridge Road and Quail Run Road, the other near the intersection of Coleman Bridge Road and Bethcar Church Road. Time estimated by radar.
Tornado sighted near Rankin St and Beattys Bridge Rd heading northeast toward Hwy 421 and Point Caswell Rd.
Fire Chief reports trees down on mobile home. No injuries reported.

Approximate beginning of tornado path. A brief, but strong, short-track tornado occurred on the northeast side of Candor in between Brutonville Road and I-73. Drone images and video provided by Eagle Springs Fire Chief assisted in determining the start point between Cherry Circle and Hurricane Drive where a significant number of uprooted and snapped trees occurred. The tornado quickly continued to track roughly northeast where significant damage occurred to a community center which had 3 of its exterior walls collapsed and several more softwood trees were snapped; consistent with high-end EF-1 to low-end EF-2 damage. The tornado continued across a small pond and snapped about 10 hardwood/softwood trees and removed a large portion of roof covering from a residence near Etta Drive. From this point, the tornado quickly lifted, not before snapping small branches, before reaching I-73 with no visible damage from drone footage to the northeast.

Storm survey found evidence of an EF-2 tornado with estimated peak winds of 115 to 125 mph. The tornado was estimated to be 150 yards wide and 24.43 miles long. The tornado path was found from Wallace to Potters Hill. It should be noted that the tornado may have briefly lifted up at times, and may have been an inconstant path especially near Beulaville toward Potters Hill. The most consistent, concentrated damage was found from west of Wallace, northeast to just west of Chinquapin. At the peak, radar indicated debris lofted as high as at least 12,000 ft, but potentially as high as 16,000 ft.
Storm spotters showed video of tornado on the ground near highway 37. Radar confirmed debris as well.

Approximate beginning of tornado path. The tornado occurred along a 3.2 mile-long discontinuous path, as it momentarily touched down and lifted several times before finally dissipating at the end of the indicated path. Damage consisted mainly of snapped and uprooted trees, large tree branches broken off, minor shingle and roof damage to several homes or structures, many fences blown over, and several power poles that were snapped and downed. There was also damage to patio furniture and signage at a service station at the intersection of Hwy 36 and Hwy 70 in Clayton. The max wind speed was 85 mph which is an EF-0 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale (EF Scale).

NWS survey team confirmed an EF-1 tornado in northern Aiken County. A tornado touched down just southeast of Bethcar Church Rd. It quickly strengthened and moved northwestward, causing mostly tree damage along its path. The most significant damage was noted beginning alone Coleman Bridge Rd and continuing along Quail Run Rd where numerous trees were uprooted or snapped. The tornado continued causing damage as it moved northwestward, crossing Kennedy Dr and Camp Rawls Rd with sporadic tree damage noted. The tornado likely lifted in a swampy area north of Eagerton Rd where the final snapped/uprooted trees were noted.

911 call center reported numerous trees and power lines down along Miller Creek Rd. Damage was likely due to a tornado. Time was estimated via radar data.
Picture of ongoing tornado near Effingham Highway. Spotter noted trees were being shredded by the tornado.

A short lived EF-1 tornado developed just south of Beaver Creek Rd, causing EF-1 damage as it crossed the road and moved northeastward. It eventually crossed a small section of the lake before lifting on the northern shoreline. Total path length: 1.07 miles Peak width: 50 yards Time on ground: 1 minute.

SCEMD reported four homes located along the 11000 block of Burtons Ferry Hwy with damage likely due to a tornado. They reported three of the homes with major damage and one destroyed. No injuries were reported. Time was estimated via radar data.
Storm spotters showed video of tornado on the ground west of Kline. Radar confirmed debris as well.

NWS storm survey team confirmed an EF-1 tornado in southern Barnwell County. A tornado developed south of Boiling Springs Rd, east of Shepherd Rd., moved to the north across a large heavily wooded field, before dissipating near Poplar Road. The tornado snapped numerous hardwood trees.

A short lived EF-1 tornado developed near the West Regional Library and traveled northeastward. Several trees were snapped in the library parking lot and in the adjacent neighborhood to the north. No structural damage was apparent during the survey, suggesting the strongest winds remained at treetop level.

Storm survey found evidence of an EF-1 tornado with estimated peak winds of 90 to 100 mph. The tornado was estimated to be 125 yards wide and 3.52 miles long. A debris signature was noted on radar, with debris estimated up to 6,000 ft to 8,000 ft.

NWS Storm Survey confirmed a brief EF-0 Tornado that crossed US421 between Matthews Rd and Willard Rd. Path length 0.18 miles, width 30 yards. Time on ground approx 1 minute.

A long-track tornado path was found from Wallace to Potters Hill. It should be noted that the tornado may have briefly lifted up at times, and may have been an inconstant path especially near Beulaville toward Potters Hill. The most consistent, concentrated damage was found from west of Wallace, northeast to just west of Chinquapin. At the peak, radar indicated debris lofted as high as at least 12,000 ft, but potentially as high as 16,000 ft.

NWS Survey Team confirmed an EF-0 tornado south southeast of Captolo, GA. A weak tornado briefly touched down near Wind Mill Road, southeast of Captolo, GA, before moving north-northeast and dissipating just north of Limesink Road. Its track was periodically visible across open grass fields. Tornado damage was minor and limited to the breakage of large branches from both hardwood and softwood trees. The tin roof was pealed back on a standalone garage.
Multiple trees down in this vicinity of Skibo Road and Morganton Road. Suspected beginning of tornado track based on initial reports.

NWS storm survey team confirmed an EF-0 tornado with an estimated peak wind speed of 85 mph near the intersection of Clito Rd and Rough Rider Rd in eastern Bulloch County. The tornado occurred from 2:12 PM to 2:13 PM. Please see the Public Information Statement for additional details.

NWS survey team confirmed an EF-1 tornado in west central Burke County. A tornado touched down in the swampland south of Highway 80 near rocky Creek. It moved northeast across Highway 80 and Abrams Rd, turning north and crossing Forest Hill Rd before lifting. Significant damage occurred at a residential farmstead on Hwy 80, including roof damage, multiple large trees uprooted, toppled portions of a center-pivot irrigation system, and multiple 18-wheeler trailers toppled over. The rest of the damage was mainly trees and limbs.

Emergency management reported a brief tornado touched down in Fort Stockton near the intersection of Ryan and Young Streets. The tornado tracked past the Pecos County Courthouse and lifted in James Rooney Memorial Park. A NWS Survey Team found damage to metal roofs and tree branches consistent with a high-end EF-0 tornado.

NWS Survey Team confired an EF-1 tornado in northern Allendale County. A tornado touched down in the wooded area between Miller Creek Road and Yackin Road, rapidly moving north across Camp Jackson Road. It dissipated just east of the Camp Jackson facility, short of the Barnwell County line. Impact was primarily limited to forested areas, with high winds snapping and uprooting clusters of hardwood and softwood trees.
Picture of ongoing tornado near Effingham Highway.

A brief, weak dusty tornadic circulation, lasting one minute or less, developed with the dust column extending to a rotating cloud base beneath a supercell thunderstorm updraft. Numerous video and pictures of this event were captured by storm chasers.
Large tree limbs damaged a couple of homes with power lines also down.
Several reports of storm damage including 18 wheeler flipped, cars lifted and dropped, roof damage, power outages and trees down around the Walmart and Sams Club along Skibo Road.

The start of the Linden, NC tornado based on NWS storm survey. Maximum winds of 105 mph (EF-1) occurred along Hungry Creek Drive where several windows were blown out of a residence. The tornado tracked along a nearly continuous path for almost 1.25 miles.
A 911 call center reported roof damage possibly to multiple homes near Hilltop Lane at Savannah Hwy. A downed power pole was also reported. Damage was likely due to a tornado.

NWS survey team confirmed an EF-1 tornado in Barnwell County. A tornado developed along Hwy 278 south of Mount Olive Cir, then continued north into the City of Barnwell, before turning northwest through Long Branch and dissipating just north of downtown Williston. The tornado produced sporadic tree damage along its path, with the most intense damage occurring in a wooded area along a field south of Freedom Road where numerous large hardwood trees were snapped and uprooted. The tornado lifted on the north side of Williston near Wilton Drive.

Corrects previous tornado report from 3 NE Fort Stockton. Trained spotter and Pecos County EM reported a tornado NE of Fort Stockton. The tornado pulled metal wall panels from a building and overturned a small shed.
Emergency manager reports one building destroyed and another severely damaged along with several large trees snapped in the Hurricane Drive and Hillview street areas.

Approximate end of tornado path. The tornado occurred along a 3.2 mile-long discontinuous path, as it momentarily touched down and lifted several times before finally dissipating at the end of the indicated path. Damage consisted mainly of snapped and uprooted trees, large tree branches broken off, minor shingle and roof damage to several homes or structures, many fences blown over, and several power poles that were snapped and downed. There was also damage to patio furniture and signage at a service station at the intersection of Hwy 36 and Hwy 70 in Clayton. The max wind speed was 85 mph which is an EF-0 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale (EF Scale).

NWS Survey Team confirmed an EF-1 tornado in eastern Screven County, GA. The tornado touched down just south of Hwy 21 near Ogeechee Creek before dissipating just north of Old Poor Robin Road. It produced significant tree damage along its path with numerous large hardwood and softwood trees being either snapped off or completely uprooted. One mobile home suffered major damage as a large hardwood tree fell on it. Several cars were also crushed from trees falling on them.
Trained spotter and Pecos County EM reported a tornado NE of Fort Stockton. Preliminary reports of damage.
Numerous reports with video and drone footage of several destroyed homes, flipped farm equipment, and considerable tree-powerline damage along highway 80 west of Waynesboro.
Tornado crossing Miller Creek Rd on live stream, which resulted in downed trees and powerlines.
Numerous trees and power poles downed near Old Savannah Hwy and Hwy 21 likely due to tornado. Damage was estimated to be about 200 yards wide.
Numerous mature hardwood and pine trees downed, snapped and twisted on Beaver Creek Road, just south of Pea Ridge Road. Damage was coincident with a radar TDS.
Newberry dispatch reported trees down along Old Blair Road. KCAE confirmed debris signature at this time and location.

The start of the Bonnie Doone tornado path based on NWS storm survey. Maximum winds of 115 mph (EF-2) occurred on a short quarter-mile section between the Walmart and Sams Club along Skibo Road while otherwise producing EF-0 to EF-1 damage along a discontinuous path for nearly 5.5 miles.
Fire Chief reports tornado on the ground near Highway 21, causing tree tops to be shredded. Live stream video also shows downed trees and debris being lofted into the air.

tracks.note: A tornado touched down in the wooded area between Miller Creek Road and Yackin Road, rapidly moving north across Camp Jackson Road. It dissipated just east of the Camp Jackson facility, short of the Barnwell County line. Impact was primarily limited to forested areas, with high winds snapping and uprooting clusters of hardwood and softwood trees.

A National Weather Service storm survey determined that an EF-1 tornado with maximum wind speeds of 95 mph occurred just west of Kline. The tornado developed south of Boiling Springs Rd, east of Shepherd Rd., moved to the north across a large heavily wooded field, before dissipating near Poplar Road. The tornado snapped numerous hardwood trees. This tornado was likely associated with a supercell that spawned multiple tornadoes.

A National Weather Service storm survey determined that an EF-2 tornado with maximum wind speeds of 115 mph occurred in Barnwell. The tornado developed along Hwy 278 south of Mount Olive Cir, then continued north into the City of Barnwell, before turning northwest through Long Branch and just north of downtown Williston. The tornado produced sporadic tree damage along its path, with the most intense damage occurring in a wooded area along a field south of Freedom Road where numerous large hardwood trees were snapped and uprooted. There is also evidence that a few wooden power poles were snapped.  The tornado lifted on the north side of Williston near Wilton Drive. This tornado was likely associated with a supercell that spawned multiple tornadoes.

A tornado touched down in the swampland south of Highway 80 near rocky Creek. It moved northeast across Highway 80 and Abrams Rd, turning north and crossing Forest Hill Rd before lifting. Significant damage occurred at a residential farmstead on Hwy 80, including roof damage, multiple large trees uprooted, toppled portions of a center-pivot irrigation system, and multiple 18-wheeler trailers toppled over. The rest of the damage was mainly trees and limbs.

East Arcadia Tornado confirmed with a combination of damage and video provided by a resident north of East Arcadia. The tornado was broad and evidence suggested that it made intermittent contact with the ground, remaining mostly elevated along the path.

On Saturday, October 10th, an EF1 tornado touched down just southeast of Bethcar Church Rd. It quickly strengthened and moved northwestward, causing mostly tree damage along its path. The most significant damage was noted beginning alone Coleman Bridge Rd and continuing along Quail Run Rd where numerous trees were uprooted or snapped. The tornado continued causing damage as it moved northwestward, crossing Kennedy Dr and Camp Rawls Rd with sporadic tree damage noted. The tornado likely lifted in a swampy area north of Eagerton Rd where the final snapped/uprooted trees were noted.

The tornado crossed Highway 301 west of Gravel Hill Road, causing some of the most significant damage. In total, four homes were impacted: one sustained destruction of aluminum roofing material and a front porch; another had complete roof and outer wall failure on a rear addition; and the other two sustained minor roofing damage. An outbuilding and two carports were also destroyed. The tornado then continued north through a heavily wooded area, but additional tree damage occurred just west of Moultry Loop and on Revolutionary Trail.

A weak tornado briefly touched down near Wind Mill Road, southeast of Captolo, GA, before moving north-northeast and dissipating just north of Limesink Road. Its track was periodically visible across open grass fields. Tornado damage was minor and limited to the breakage of large branches from both hardwood and softwood trees.  The  tin roof was pealed back on a standalone garage.

A rapidly intensifying tornado touched down just south of Highway 21 near Ogeechee Creek before dissipating just north of Old Poor Robin Road in far eastern Screven County, GA. The tornado produced significant tree damage along its path with numerous large hardwood and softwood trees being either snapped off or completely uprooted. One mobile home suffered major damage as a large hardwood tree fell on it. Several cars were also crushed from trees falling on them. Tree damage was observed on parts of Old Poor Robin Road, Poor Robin Road, Wiseman Road and Highway 21.

The tornado occurred at a property along Roseland Rd east of Joe Brown Hwy South. Several open farm buildings were destroyed due to roof uplift and subsequent wall failure. Debris was scattered along a narrow path. An empty grain bin was also lifted off its foundation and shifted. Sheet metal roofing was scattered along the path including high into tree canopies and into an adjacent field beyond the grove of trees.

A long-track storm produced mostly EF-0 to EF-1 damage, including a short, quarter-mile stretch of EF-2 damage with maximum wind speeds estimated at 115 mph. The tornado touched down near the intersection of Skibo and Morganton roads, knocking down several trees and removing a couple of HVAC units from the Burlington Shoes store within a strip mall. The tornado then likely lifted briefly before touching down again and intensifying near the Walmart along Skibo Road, where it removed nearly 10 HVAC units from the roof, causing minor damage as they tumbled across it. The tornado continued between two hotels, where it bent and collapsed poles, damaged roofs, and rolled a car or two. As the tornado continued through the Sam’s Club parking lot, roughly a dozen cars were toppled or lifted, and one minor injury was reported. A short-lived tornado with maximum wind speeds of 105 mph initially developed along Ramsey Street near Linden, NC, and continued to track northeast. The most significant damage occurred as the tornado crossed through a residential area between Glenmont Creek Place, Hungry Creek Drive, and Rainy Beck Way. Several homes had minor roof and fence damage; however, a select few along Hungry Creek Drive sustained high-end EF-1 damage, where 50% of the windows were blown out, fence posts set in poured concrete were pulled from the ground, and wind-blown timber punctured exterior walls. The tornado continued tracking northeast into an open area, where drone photos provided by the Harnett County Deputy Fire Marshal revealed a noticeable path through a dormant cornfield and a section of downed or snapped softwood trees in a field north of Horseshoe Bend Road. A long track supercell produced an initial weak tornado near the intersection of Clito Road and Rough Rider Road in eastern Bulloch County. The National Weather Service received a witness report of a tornado on the ground and, upon conducting a ground and drone survey, found that large trees were uprooted in a convergent pattern, large branches were snapped, and a crop pivot was damaged along the path where the tornado briefly touched down in the area.

A tornado associated with the outer bands of Hurricane Isaias moved onshore near the intersection of US 98 and State Road 65 east of Eastpoint in Franklin County. The tornado was captured on video, provided by a local media outlet. The tornado moved inland approximately one mile, causing minor damage to several homes along State Road 65 and Michael Way before dissipating in a forested area.
